# Ancient's Privilege
Ancients may, at any point mid-round, change the Honor Code or allow actions that would normally go against it. Ancients must state the change over the radio, along with who it is intended for.
Ancients who change the Honor Code for a round may still be reported for violating the [textlink="Spirit of the Whitelist" link="AU14YautjaHonorCodeSpirit"].
The main purpose of ancients is to prevent Honor Code breaks before they happen, or to give instructions on how to rectify them. You may also ask the ancients for advice if you are unsure whether something is acceptable under the Honor Code.
Their changes can range from declaring prey in an area dishonorable to boarding the human ship. In the latter case, the ancients should give clear directions on what the Yautja should do aboard and when to leave.
## Good examples of using Ancient's Privilege - Allowing Yautja to kill (not permakill) members of CIC because they launched an OB directly on the lodge, away from any xenomorph front or fortifications, out of spite for the Yautja. The overseeing elder also instructs the Yautja not to use explosive weapons, so game-critical equipment in CIC isn't destroyed. - Permitting an eager but un-huntable human to be hunted and thralled after they have shown outstanding roleplay.
## Bad examples of using Ancient's Privilege - Singling out a player and marking them for death with little to no reason. - Allowing Yautja to build lodges in high-traffic areas, like hydroponics on LV-624.
